title: Sheaves on a localized site as sheaves over a sheafified representable
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ its category of sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $U$ be an object and give $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $h_U(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,U)$ with restriction by precomposition and let $h_U^\#$ be its sheafification with unit $\eta:h_U\to h_U^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The category $\Sh(\mathcal C)/h_U^\#$ has objects sheaf maps $p:F\to h_U^\#$ and arrows sheaf maps commuting with these maps. There is an equivalence $E_U:\Sh(\mathcal C/U)\simeq\Sh(\mathcal C)/h_U^\#$ whose quasi-inverse sends $(F,p)$ to the sheaf
$$ (X\xrightarrow{a}U)\longmapsto\{s\in F(X):p_X(s)=\eta_X(a)\}, $$
with restrictions induced by those of $F$; on arrows it restricts the component maps to these fibres. Concretely $E_U(H)$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $X\mapsto\coprod_{a:X\to U}H(X\xrightarrow{a}U)$, with restriction $(a,s)\mapsto(a\circ b,H(b)(s))$ along $b:Y\to X$, equipped with its map to $h_U^\#$ induced by $(a,s)\mapsto a$. The equivalence has natural unit and counit isomorphisms. No subcanonical-topology or existence-of-all-fibre-products assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the fibre functor $R$. For $(F,p)$ put $R(F,p)(X,a)=\{s\in F(X):p_X(s)=\eta_X(a)\}$, and restrict along $b:(Y,ab)\to(X,a)$ using $F(b)$. Naturality of $p$ and $\eta$ preserves the fibre condition. For a covering of $(X,a)$ the underlying family covers $X$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A matching family in these fibres glues uniquely in $F(X)$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; its image under $p$ and $\eta_X(a)$ agree on the cover, hence agree in the sheaf $h_U^\#$. Thus the amalgamation lies in the fibre, proving the sheaf condition. A map over $h_U^\#$ preserves each fibre, and its component restrictions respect identities and composition. This defines $R$ on objects and arrows.

source.place: Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek), first construction of the fibre sheaf; Section 00XZ (section-localize), localized coverings.

proof.text: For a sheaf $H$ on $\mathcal C/U$ define $P_H(X)=\coprod_{a:X\to U}H(X,a)$ and $q_H:P_H\to h_U$ by $q_H(a,s)=a$. Along $b:Y\to X$ set $(a,s)|_Y=(ab,H(b)(s))$; the functor laws for $H$ prove the presheaf laws and naturality of $q_H$. Let $\theta_H:P_H\to P_H^\#$ be the sheafification unit. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends $\eta q_H$ uniquely to $\bar q_H:P_H^\#\to h_U^\#$. Set $E(H)=(P_H^\#,\bar q_H)$. For $f:H\to H'$ the presheaf map $(a,s)\mapsto(a,f_{X,a}(s))$ induces a unique sheaf map $E(f)$; uniqueness of extensions proves compatibility with the structure maps and the identity and composition laws. This is exactly the concrete functor required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek), disjoint-union functor; lemma-describe-j-shriek in Section 00XZ; universal property of sheafification.

proof.text: Define $u_H:H\to R E(H)$ by $s\mapsto\theta_{H,X}(a,s)$ at $(X,a)$; it lies in the fibre because $\bar q_H\theta_H(a,s)=\eta_X(a)$. This map is natural under restrictions. It is componentwise injective: equal images of $(a,s)$ and $(a,t)$ in $P_H^\#(X)$ imply equality of these pairs on a covering of $X$ by the local-equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. The covering lifts to $(X,a)$, where separatedness of $H$ gives $s=t$. For surjectivity let $z\in P_H^\#(X)$ satisfy $\bar q_H(z)=\eta_X(a)$. The local-representative clause of the same node supplies a covering $b_i:X_i\to X$ and pairs $(a_i,s_i)\in P_H(X_i)$ representing $z|_{X_i}$. Their images satisfy $\eta(a_i)=\eta(ab_i)$. Apply the local-equality clause to the presheaf $h_U$ to refine each covering member until $a_i=ab_i$ on that refinement. Composition of covers gives a cover of $X$ and all these $s_i$ now lie in $H(X_i,ab_i)$. On overlaps they have the same image under $u_H$, namely the restriction of $z$; the injectivity already proved, applied to the overlap object over $U$, proves equality. Glue in $H$ to obtain $s\in H(X,a)$. The images of $u_H(s)$ and $z$ agree on the cover, so separatedness of $P_H^\#$ gives $u_H(s)=z$. Therefore $u_H$ is an isomorphism, with inverse given componentwise by these unique preimages. For a restriction $b:(Y,ab)\to(X,a)$, naturality gives $u_{H,Y}(H(b)(s))=R E(H)(b)(u_{H,X}(s))$; uniqueness of preimages under $u_{H,Y}$ therefore proves that the componentwise inverses commute with $b$. Only pullbacks of covering arrows were used.

source.place: Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek), first inverse comparison; agent local-section proof using Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification) and Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus).

proof.text: For $(F,p)$ define $t:P_{R(F,p)}\to F$ by $t_X(a,s)=s$. Naturality of restrictions is immediate and $p\,t=\eta q$. Extend uniquely through sheafification to $c_{F,p}:E R(F,p)\to(F,p)$ using [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; the extension is over $h_U^\#$ because the two structure maps agree after the sheafification unit. Prove componentwise injectivity of $c$: if $z,z'\in P_{R(F,p)}^\#(X)$ have equal images, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] supplies local pair representatives for each. Refine to a common covering (pull back the second cover along members of the first and compose), obtaining representatives $(a,s)$ and $(a',s')$ over each member with $s=s'$ in $F$. Their fibre conditions give $\eta(a)=p(s)=p(s')=\eta(a')$. The local-equality clause applied to $h_U$ refines once more until $a=a'$. The representatives are then equal as pairs, so $z$ and $z'$ agree on this covering. Separatedness of $P_{R(F,p)}^\#$ gives $z=z'$. This argument does not identify $h_U$ with $h_U^\#$.

source.place: Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek), second inverse comparison; agent injectivity proof using Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification) and Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus).

proof.text: Prove componentwise surjectivity of $c_{F,p}$. For $s\in F(X)$ apply the local-representative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to $p_X(s)\in h_U^\#(X)$. It gives a covering $b_i:X_i\to X$ and arrows $a_i:X_i\to U$ with $\eta(a_i)=p(s)|_{X_i}=p(s|_{X_i})$. Consequently $(a_i,s|_{X_i})\in P_{R(F,p)}(X_i)$. Their sheafification images $z_i$ map under $c$ to $s|_{X_i}$. On every overlap the two restrictions of $z_i$ have equal images under $c$, so the injectivity proved in step 4 forces equality. Glue the $z_i$ in $P_{R(F,p)}^\#$; the resulting $z$ has $c(z)=s$ by separatedness of $F$. Thus $c$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. Its inverse is also over $h_U^\#$ by composing the structure-map identity with the inverse.

source.place: Tag 00Y1 (lemma-essential-image-j-shriek), second inverse comparison; agent surjectivity proof using Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification).

proof.text: The maps $u_H$ are natural in $H$: both sides of the naturality square send $s\in H(X,a)$ to $\theta_{H',X}(a,f(s))$. The maps $c_{F,p}$ are natural in maps over $h_U^\#$: precomposition with the sheafification unit makes both sides send $(a,s)$ to the image of $s$, so uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] proves the square. Hence steps 3 and 5 give natural isomorphisms $\mathrm{id}\cong R E$ and $E R\cong\mathrm{id}$. The triangle on $R(F,p)$ sends a fibre section $s$ first to the image of $(a,s)$ and then back to $s$. The triangle on $E(H)$, precomposed with $\theta_H$, sends $(a,s)$ first to $(a,\theta_H(a,s))$ and then to $\theta_H(a,s)$; uniqueness of extensions proves that it is the identity. Thus $E$ and $R$ form the stated equivalence with natural unit and counit. All constructions use only disjoint unions of sets, sheafification, and gluing along coverings; no subcanonicity or unrestricted fibre products have been introduced.
